title: PHD: Parallel Huffman Decoder on FPGA for Extreme Performance and Energy Efficiency
problem: Huffman decoding requires efficient management of fine-grained parallelism with inter-codeword dependencies on memory-constrained FPGAs while exploiting subsequence-level parallelism.
motivation: Huffman decoding is crucial for data compression and requires efficient hardware acceleration to achieve extreme performance and energy efficiency.
method: PHD speeds up decoding of Huffman-compressed data (a compression technique that shrinks file sizes) by working around a key constraint: each decoded symbol depends on the previous one, which normally prevents parallelization. It uses self-synchronization to identify parallelizable work at three levels—individual bits, groups of symbols (subsequences), and larger data blocks (tiles)—and stores the decoding rule table (codebook) using a two-tier memory design optimized for the FPGA's limited memory. An optimization called ONCE MORE further speeds decoding by reducing loop iterations.
key_novelty: PHD is the first FPGA Huffman decoder that enables parallel work despite each decoded symbol depending on the previous one, by using self-synchronization at three scales (bits, subsequences, and tiles), along with smart memory management and loop optimization.
contributions: First self-synchronization-based parallel Huffman decoder on FPGA
Multi-level parallelism design spanning bit-level, subsequence-level, and tile-level granularities
Hybrid memory system for efficient codebook storage addressing on-chip memory constraints
ONCE MORE optimization to reduce decoding loop iterations
primary_theme: Efficient FPGA acceleration of parallel Huffman decoding
